title: Hosted API: Customer Impact Simulator & What-If Runbook for Intake Prioritization (chat/streaming/tool-calls/structured outputs)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a lightweight simulator and an associated runbook for PMs and SREs to run 'what-if' scenarios when triaging Hosted API feature requests from enterprise customers. The simulator will estimate latency, cost delta, and regression risk (quality drop probability) for proposed feature combinations across chat, streaming, tool/function calls, and structured outputs. The runbook codifies decision thresholds for routing requests into priority lanes, gated pilots, or decline/fallback. Purpose: reduce triage cycle time and standardize intake recommendations presented to sales and customers.
motivation: We frequently make triage decisions with incomplete quantitative signals. Sales and CSMs ask for fast, defensible answers on whether a request can be supported in Hosted, Dedicated, or Private modes and what trade-offs (cost/latency/quality) look like. A simulator plus runbook will (1) speed decisions, (2) provide repeatable guidance to engineering about suggested implementation scope, and (3) create transparent artifacts for customer conversations and SLA negotiations.
scope: Lightweight simulator UI (spreadsheet-style) that accepts request parameters: expected rps, avg tokens per request, streaming vs batch, tool-call frequency, structured-output constraints
Back-end cost & latency model derived from empirical perf data (hosted benchmarks + recent runtime telemetry)
Quality risk estimator: heuristics mapping model/quantization choices and prompt complexity to regression risk
Runbook: step-by-step triage flow with recommended actions and escalation paths
Exportable scenario summaries for customer-facing proposals
Integration hooks: link to intake ticket and to existing cost dashboards (read-only)
Minimum MVP does not include automated routing changes or enforcement — this is decision support only
acceptance_criteria: PMs can create a scenario for a customer request and produce a summarized PDF with estimated monthly token cost delta, median p95 latency, and a regression risk tier
Simulator uses host telemetry (last 30 days) to parameterize latency and batching assumptions
Runbook defines clear thresholds (low/medium/high) across cost, latency, and quality that map to recommended intake lanes: self-serve, canary pilot, dedicated consult, or decline
At least two enterprise intake cases from sales are validated end-to-end with the simulator and the runbook and recorded in the ticket
Simulator UI is accessible from the intake ticket and links back to the ticket ID in exported PDFs
design_notes: Prefer spreadsheet-like UI with formula transparency rather than opaque ML model
Show confidence bands: optimistic/median/pessimistic scenarios based on traffic and token variance
Make all assumptions visible (e.g., batching window, kv-cache hit rate, quantization level) so eng and research can dispute and improve numbers
Keep localization and currency formatting flexible for EU/APAC later
engineering_notes: Initial cost model will be a parametric function: cost = tokens * (base_unit_cost + batching_savings(token_window) + quantization_multiplier)
Latency model will use percentiles pulled from perf-dashboard via read-only API; fallback to stored bench values if dashboard rate-limited
Quality risk will be heuristic-based for MVP: model_size, quantization_level, prompt_complexity => risk score (low/med/high)
MVP backend is a small Flask service with a single endpoint that returns scenario JSON; UI will be static React linked from ticket
Auth: simulator view should respect internal RBAC; no customer-facing auth in MVP
risks_and_tradeoffs: Estimates may be wrong for corner production patterns; we'll include confidence bands and explicit caveats
Heuristic quality risk may under/overestimate for novel prompts — requires iterative calibration with research
Maintenance burden: models and parameters must be refreshed after runtime changes; require a small monthly upkeep task
Avoid over-automation: this tool supports decisions but should not auto-change routing or SLAs in MVP
